work_or_witness: Epic of Gilgamesh · George 2003, Vol. I, Tablet I, lines 1–62 (Gilgameš and Uruk opening)
definition: The royal title relevant to Gilgameš’s authority in Uruk; it is retained as a Mesopotamian title rather than mapped to a universal ruler package.
cultural_caution: Do not infer that the poem is a direct document of one historical Uruk kingship or reduce ancient Mesopotamian royal ideology to a generic fantasy monarchy.

citations.locator: George 2003, Vol. I, Tablet I, lines 1–62 (Gilgameš and Uruk opening)
supports: The Standard Babylonian opening frames Gilgameš through kingship and Uruk.

work_or_witness: Epic of Gilgamesh · George 2003, Vol. I, Tablet V, lines 1–100 (approach to Ḫumbaba and Cedar Forest)
definition: A source-native numinous/terrifying quality associated in the Cedar Forest episode with Ḫumbaba’s fearful presence; it is not treated as a transferable spell school or energy meter.
cultural_caution: Translation varies (‘aura,’ ‘terror,’ ‘radiance,’ ‘splendour’). Do not turn this Mesopotamian concept into generic ‘magic power’ without contextual analysis.

citations.locator: George 2003, Vol. I, Tablet V, lines 1–100 (approach to Ḫumbaba and Cedar Forest)
supports: Tablet V’s encounter supplies the immediate epic context for Ḫumbaba’s terrifying numinous quality.

work_or_witness: Epic of Gilgamesh · George 2003, Vol. I, Tablet XI, lines 1–34 (Gilgameš questions Uta-napišti’s exceptional condition); Epic of Gilgamesh · SOAS BAPLar, Tablet XI, lines 1–34, transcription and translation after George
definition: A core life/mortality concept in the Uta-napišti episode and in the name Uta-napišti (‘he found life’); it is not a game-life statistic.
cultural_caution: Do not equate napīštu mechanically with soul, hit points, biological life, or a universal doctrine of immortality.

citations.locator: George 2003, Vol. I, Tablet XI, lines 1–34 (Gilgameš questions Uta-napišti’s exceptional condition)
supports: The tablet frames Gilgameš’s inquiry into Uta-napišti’s exceptional life.

citations.locator: SOAS BAPLar, Tablet XI, lines 1–34, transcription and translation after George
supports: Accessible line-specific transcription of the encounter.

work_or_witness: Epic of Gilgamesh · George 2003, Vol. I, Tablet X, lines 200–320 (Urshanabi and crossing toward Uta-napišti)
definition: The perilous waters crossed with Urshanabi on the route to Uta-napišti; retained as a named source-native liminal feature, not a generic afterlife biome.
cultural_caution: The phrase’s narrative and cosmological force belongs to this tablet reconstruction; it should not be used to impose a fixed Mesopotamian map of the afterlife.

citations.locator: George 2003, Vol. I, Tablet X, lines 200–320 (Urshanabi and crossing toward Uta-napišti)
supports: The journey narrative identifies the Waters of Death and Urshanabi’s crossing.

work_or_witness: Epic of Gilgamesh · George 2003, Vol. I, Tablet V, lines 1–300 (Cedar Forest and Ḫumbaba episode)
definition: The Cedar Forest in the Standard Babylonian expedition, guarded by Ḫumbaba; it is a specific epic locale and not promoted to a visualization node.
cultural_caution: Do not flatten the Cedar Forest into a generic enchanted forest or assume all related landscape traditions are identical.

citations.locator: George 2003, Vol. I, Tablet V, lines 1–300 (Cedar Forest and Ḫumbaba episode)
supports: The tablet supplies the specific expedition and guardian context.

work_or_witness: Epic of Gilgamesh · George 2003, Vol. I, Tablet III, lines 1–190
definition: The collective advising body that counsels Gilgamesh and entrusts him to Enkidu's guidance before the Cedar Forest expedition. It is retained as an institution/collective term, not a character node.
cultural_caution: A collective textual actor is not converted into an individual, a modern civic institution, or a generic fantasy council.

citations.locator: George 2003, Vol. I, Tablet III, lines 1–190
supports: The Elders of Uruk counsel Gilgamesh and entrust him to Enkidu's guidance before the expedition.
